correctness.rationale: The reset-event Markov kernel is reconstructed from Bessel-squared occupation probabilities, its eigenvalue from a telescoping Bessel flux identity, and its strict monotonicity in both unscaled parameters follows from positivity. The classical Bessel–Legendre Laplace transform plus the Schläfli Q integral give an exact positive Abel transform and a probability density that is the pushforward of \(\mathrm{Exp}(1)\) under \(W_a=2a\sinh(E/(2a))\). Pointwise ordering of W_a yields strict all-size monotonicity. The density admits an L1-uniform inverse-square Taylor expansion with integrable \(O(a^{-4})\) remainder, giving the stated explicit negative coefficient for all \(z\ge0\). 81 numerical assertions support independent representations, asymptotic coefficient, and boundary values; the analytic proof establishes the infinite claims.

value.rationale: The reset-site sign is a concrete physically measurable record whose full sequence of correlations cannot be reconstructed from the stationary spatial marginal alone. The exact coupling gives a rigorous distance–rate tradeoff and ordering at every finite size, not just a large-distance limit. The sharp signed uniform finite-distance correction quantifies convergence to ballistic scaling and shows which side the approximation lies on. This is a natural transport/correlation question for the source protocol, distinct from a textbook transformation of a free-walk limit.
